note.subject: french
note.title: Pronunciation
note.overview: Learn the school vocabulary, then use it in the applied questions. Work only on the section assigned in class.
learningGoals: Recall meanings accurately and apply the relevant grammar in context.

workedExamples.prompt: In chat, which English sound is closest to French ch?
workedExamples.why: In this word ch represents the sh sound.

workedExamples.prompt: In montagne, which sound does gn represent?
workedExamples.why: Gn is a palatal nasal, approximately ny; it is not pronounced as separate g and n.

workedExamples.prompt: Are final consonants always silent in French?
workedExamples.why: They are often silent, but exceptions and liaison exist. The school mnemonic is a guide, not an absolute rule.

workedExamples.prompt: In the word français, what sound does ç make?
workedExamples.why: The cedilla keeps the soft s sound before a.

detailedExplanation: Many final consonants are silent, but this is not universal. Liaison may make a normally silent final consonant audible before the next vowel.
Final unaccented e is often silent. É is pronounced. Do not assume every written e or -ent is pronounced.
Keep u and ou distinct; oi commonly sounds like wa. French nasal vowels cannot be represented accurately by one English spelling. The booklet’s comparisons are approximate memory aids.
The booklet groups en, an and on together; en/an and on are different nasal vowels. Listen to teacher models rather than merging them.

quickCheck.question: In chat, which English sound is closest to French ch?
In montagne, which sound does gn represent?
Are final consonants always silent in French?

retrievalPlan: Introduce 3 to 5 unfamiliar words at a time.
Use one question per concept per session; mix older concepts with new work.
Revisit errors after 2 days and 7 days.
